rawAnswer: {"findings":[{"kind":"defect","severity":"high","title":"Constructor fallback now prefers fewest parameters for all types","detail":"The requirement does not ask for this. When no constructor has [SerializationConstructor], constructors with equal accessibility used to be tried from most parameters to fewest. They are now tried from fewest to most. This applies to every type, not only suppressed ones. A type with a public parameterless constructor and a public constructor that takes its get-only keyed members will now get the parameterless constructor, because a zero-parameter constructor always matches. The generated formatter will then never set those get-only members, so they come back as defaults after deserialization (silent data loss). The constructor-related diagnostics and the generated output also change for non-suppressed types, which breaks N2 (existing snapshots and behaviour should stay the same).
